question.worked_solution:
To save time, we will keep the variable on the right-hand side as we solve. First, we rewrite the right-hand side by placing the term containing the variable first:

$$
\begin{aligned}23 & =3+5x \\ 23 & =5x+3\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $3$ from both sides:

$$
\begin{aligned}23 & =5x+3 \\ 23-3 & =5x+3-3 \\ 20 & =5x+0 \\ 20 & =5x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}20 & =5x \\ \frac{20}{5} & =\frac{5x}{5} \\ 4 & =\frac{\cancel{5}x}{\cancel{5}} \\ 4 & =x\end{aligned}
$$

Since $4=x,$ we conclude that the solution is $x=4.$
